requirements.text: Append framed checksummed records before applying writes; acknowledge only at the selected sync boundary.
Recover a verified snapshot and contiguous WAL suffix, stopping only at a torn tail and rejecting interior corruption.
Publish checkpoints atomically with a cut LSN and retain WAL generations until the new manifest is durable.

problem.scope: Systems-coding design for a single-process in-memory key/value store. Compare synchronous per-write WAL with group commit and generation checkpoints. Physical power-loss guarantees depend on filesystem/device behavior and require fault injection beyond bounded reference models.

evidence.testName: sync failure fails waiters stops writes and never retries fsync

acceptanceCases.given: A WAL record is appended but sync fails.
acceptanceCases.then: Fail that write, stop accepting writes and reopen from disk; never retry fsync or claim durable success.

acceptanceCases.given: A snapshot ends at LSN 2 and suffix contains 3,4 plus an incomplete tail.
acceptanceCases.then: Apply 3 and 4 once; stop at tail, but reject interior corruption or a sequence gap.
acceptanceCases.when: Replay with checksum and sequence validation.

evidence.testName: frame headers carry their own checksum so interior length damage is corruption

acceptanceCases.given: An interior frame's length header is rewritten to 1000.
acceptanceCases.then: The header checksum fails while later frames verify, so recovery reports corruption instead of dropping LSNs 3-5 as a torn tail.

acceptanceCases.given: A crash happens after the snapshot rename but before the manifest sync.
acceptanceCases.then: Recovery uses the old manifest and its retained WAL; the unpublished snapshot is ignored.

acceptanceCases.given: A checkpoint at cut 50 is written but its manifest is not yet durable.
acceptanceCases.then: Retain WAL generations through 50 and delete them only after the manifest sync.

evidence.testName: WAL framed suffix preserves tombstones rejects gaps and separates sync watermark

acceptanceCases.given: Snapshot cut is 2 with a key later deleted.
acceptanceCases.then: Preserve delete, stop at incomplete tail, reject checksum/gap, and release only waiters within the sync watermark; physical durability is untested.
acceptanceCases.when: Replay complete frames 3/4 and torn frame 5, then corrupt a frame and try a gap.

guarantees: A short write is retried or fails; it is never assumed complete.
OS-buffered append alone cannot satisfy always-sync acknowledgement, and a failed fsync is never retried into a success.
The snapshot contains exactly state through its cut.
The old manifest and logs remain until publication is durable.
Interior checksum failure is a surfaced error, not skipped data.
No acknowledged suffix is removed before a recoverable checkpoint exists.

stages.explanation: Append framed checksummed records before applying writes; acknowledge only at the selected sync boundary. durable means this LSN's framed record was fsynced before the write was applied and acknowledged; sync-failed promises nothing about persistence, and the store refuses writes until it reopens from disk. [Write-ahead logging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Write-ahead_logging) records a change before relying on its final stored form. Recovery replays durable records, so acknowledgement and flush boundaries must match the promised durability.
invariants: durable means this LSN's framed record was fsynced before the write was applied and acknowledged; sync-failed promises nothing about persistence, and the store refuses writes until it reopens from disk.
